paragraphs: Friend, here's what the Teacher wants you to know: money is a terrible thing to love, because it never says "enough." He says, "He who loves money is never satisfied by money" (Ecclesiastes 5:10). The more piles up, the more hands show up to eat it (Ecclesiastes 5:11), and the rich man ends up lying awake while the worker sleeps sweet (Ecclesiastes 5:12). I think that's the sneaky part, because chasing more feels like chasing peace, and it never gets you there.

And the Teacher doesn't let the chase off easy. Whether wealth gets hoarded or lost, a man leaves just as he came, and he takes nothing in his hands (Ecclesiastes 5:15). So what does he gain as he toils for the wind (Ecclesiastes 5:16)? Friend, I've watched a batch of cookies disappear in one evening, so trust me, you can't hold onto the good stuff by squeezing harder.

So what do you do instead? The Teacher says it is good and fitting to eat, drink and find satisfaction in your labor during the few days God has given you (Ecclesiastes 5:18). He says enjoying it is "a gift from God" (Ecclesiastes 5:19). Today, baker, do your work, enjoy what's on your plate, and receive it as a gift instead of a prize you have to keep earning.
